title: Planar tetranuclear lanthanide clusters with the Dy4 analogue displaying slow magnetic relaxation

synthesis.procedure: Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.45 g, 1 mmol) was dissolved in MeOH (20 ml) followed by addition of pivalic acid (0.1 g, 1 mmol), 3-methoxysalicylaldehyde (0.15 g, 1 mmol) and triethylamine (0.3 ml, 2 mmol) to give a light yellow solution. The mixture was stirred for 2 hours, the solvent removed, and the residue redissolved in CH2Cl2 (10 ml). Layering with Et2O afforded light yellow crystals of 1 after 1–2 days.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring then solvent removal and CH2Cl2/Et2O layering
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solvent removed; residue redissolved in CH2Cl2 (10 ml) and layered with Et2O; light yellow crystals of 1 after 1–2 days

properties.summary: Weakly antiferromagnetically coupled isotropic Gd4 butterfly. χMT is nearly temperature-independent down to ~50 K then falls, consistent with very weak exchange; two-J fit gives a tiny wing–body coupling and a small body–body J, with no isolated ground state. Magnetization at 2 K/5 T nearly saturates near the four-ion Gd(III) limit.

synthesis.procedure: Dy(NO3)3·xH2O (0.45 g, 1 mmol) was dissolved in MeOH (20 ml) followed by addition of pivalic acid (0.1 g, 1 mmol), 3-methoxysalicylaldehyde (0.15 g, 1 mmol) and triethylamine (0.3 ml, 2 mmol) to give a light yellow solution. The mixture was stirred for 2 hours, the solvent removed, and the residue redissolved in CH2Cl2 (10 ml). Layering with Et2O afforded light yellow crystals after 1–2 days (text copy refers to crystals of 1; procedure is for compound 2).

properties.summary: Anisotropic Dy4 butterfly with weak coupling. χMT decreases at low T from thermal depopulation of ligand-field states. Frequency-dependent AC out-of-phase signals below 8 K indicate probable SMM behaviour with a small effective barrier (~5 K) and fast τ0; applied DC field (3000 Oe) does not change the relaxation time, suggesting negligible zero-field QTM.
